newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson hoists Swedish shares to fresh records.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson hoists Swedish shares to fresh records.

text.p: Swedish shares broke to another record high on the index on Wednesday, dominated by gains in telecoms group Ericsson but also in forestries.
The general index toppled a one-day old high to end at 3,143.94, up 0.74 percent. Turnover totalled 4.89 billion crowns, brisk for the normally quiet summer season.
"In the end the Dow Jones dipped, which spilled over onto the Swedish market. Otherwise there are no bears and we are seeing several foreign players buying," one broker said.
Ericsson rose seven crowns to a year-high 326.5 close after better-than-expected results from rival Motorola Inc..
The forestry sector index jumped 3.25 percent after U.S. forestry stocks gained on news International Paper Co. planned to sell $1 billion worth of assets and slash 9,000 jobs.
"This, together with rumours about a strike in Canada mean a a gold rush for the industry," one broker said.
Insurance company Skandia rose five crowns to 327.5. But bears were to be found.
"We downgraded our buy recommendation to hold when the stock price reached 293 crowns," said HSBC James Capel analyst Michael Broom. "At current levels we would be pretty cautious."
